Basque

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /talo/ [t̪a.lo]
  • Rhymes: -alo, -o
  • Hyphenation: ta‧lo

Etymology 1

[edit]

From a Romance language, ultimately perhaps from Latin thallus.[1] See below for more details.

Adjective

[edit]

talo (comparative taloago, superlative taloen, excessive taloegi)

  1. chubby, plump

    Finnish

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Proto-Finnic *taloi (“farm; house”), of disputed further origin. Cognates include Estonian talu (“farm”); Northern Sami dállu (“house; farm”) is a Finnic loan.[1]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈtɑlo/, [ˈt̪ɑ̝lo̞]
    • Rhymes: -ɑlo
    • Syllabification(key): ta‧lo
    • Hyphenation(key): ta‧lo

    Noun

    [edit]

    talo

    1. house (building meant to serve as a human abode)
    2. (loosely or in compounds) building
      Synonyms: rakennus, pytinki
    3. (now rustic or historical) farm, homestead
      Synonyms: maatila, tila, farmi
    4. house, household (the people living in a house)
    5. (in compounds) company, especially one that manufactures or supplies something
      lihatalo ― meat company
    6. (chiefly informal) workplace, e.g. company or public agency, house
    7. (chiefly informal) ellipsis of taloyhtiö (“housing company”)

      Ingrian

      [edit]

      Alternative forms

      [edit]
      • taloi (dialectal)

      Etymology

      [edit]

      From Proto-Finnic *taloi, borrowed from a Baltic language. Cognates include Finnish talo and Estonian talu.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • (Ala-Laukaa) IPA(key): /ˈtɑlo/, [ˈtɑɫo̞ˑ]
      • (Soikkola) IPA(key): /ˈtɑloi̯/, [ˈtɑɫo̞i̯]
      • (Hevaha) IPA(key): /ˈtɑloi̯/, [ˈtɑɫo̞i̯]
      • Rhymes: -ɑlo, -ɑloi̯
      • Hyphenation: ta‧lo

      Noun

      [edit]

      talo

      1. house
        talon väki ― household (literally, “crowd of the house”)

      Latin

      [edit]

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

      Adapted from Middle French talon, Italian tallone, themselves from Latin tālus; by surface analysis, tālus +‎ ō (also as -ōnus).

      Alternative forms

      [edit]
      • talonus

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈtaː.lo]

      Noun

      [edit]

      tālō m (genitive tālōnis); third declension

      1. (Medieval Latin, anatomy) heel
        Synonym: calx
      Declension
      [edit]

      Third-declension noun.

      singular plural
      nominative tālō tālōnēs

            Tagalog

            [edit]

            Etymology 1

            [edit]

            From Proto-Philippine *talu, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *talu (“to lose, be defeated”). Cognate with Balinese talu (“defeated”). Unrelated to Malay takluk.

            Pronunciation

            [edit]
            • (Standard Tagalog)
              • IPA(key): /ˈtalo/ [ˈt̪aː.lo], (uncommon) /taˈlo/ [t̪ɐˈlo] (adjective)
                • Rhymes: -alo, (uncommon) -o
              • IPA(key): /ˈtalo/ [ˈt̪aː.lo] (noun)
                • Rhymes: -alo
            • Syllabification: ta‧lo

            Adjective

            [edit]

            talo or taló (Baybayin spelling ᜆᜎᜓ)

            1. defeated; beaten; surpassed; vanquished
              Nagsisiawayan ang mga manlalaro sa natalong tim.
              The players in the losing team argued with each other.
            2. lost one's bet in gambling
            Derived terms
            [edit]
            • di-mananalo
            • ikapanalo
            • ikatalo
            • ipanalo
            • magpanalo
            • magpatalo

            • manalo

            • mapanalunan
            • matalo
            • nananalo
            • natatalo
            • olats

            • pagtalo
            • panalo
            • panalunan
            • patalo
            • taluhin
            • talunan
            • talunin
            • talusaling
            • talusira
            • tumalo

            Noun

            [edit]

            talo (Baybayin spelling ᜆᜎᜓ)

            1. defeat; loss (in a contest, game, fight, etc.)
              Synonym: pagkatalo
              Antonym: panalo
            2. loser (person that fails to win)
              Synonym: talunan
            3. act of defeating
              Synonym: pagtalo
            4. (gambling) amount of money lost
            5. (business, colloquial) loss in sales
            6. (obsolete) victory; win
